ONE square detailed painterly Slavic mythology illustration of BANNIK: a very SMALL dirty elderly male bathhouse spirit with a long tangled grey beard, long hair, and conspicuously large human hands. Birch leaves from used bath brooms cover his shoulders and torso, while a modest opaque linen wrap and leaves obscure the lower body as an artistic modesty treatment. No exposed genitals. He crouches beside a great dark stove in an old wooden banya, his tiny scale clear against normal wooden buckets and benches. His gaunt wrinkled face peers fiercely through uncanny luminous pale-green STEAM, deep shadows and orange stove-glow; numinous menace appropriate to a mischievous sometimes dangerous bathhouse spirit. Entire silhouette and both hands inside frame. Realistic aged skin, wet birch leaves and timber textures, painterly encyclopedia art. No horns, wings, invented animal body, human victims, text, watermark, decorative frame or gore.
